pr_title: [GR-46536] Add jdk.internal.platform to built-in package natives
pr_comment: Do we still need the substitution introduced in #5390 with this or should that be cleaned up?

> Do we still need the substitution introduced in #5390 with this or should that be cleaned up?

Good point, @jerboaa WDYT ?

> > Do we still need the substitution introduced in #5390 with this or should that be cleaned up?
> 
> Good point, @jerboaa WDYT ?

The substitution in #5390 applies to JDK 17 and later and uses `PhysicalMemorySupport` over the native call. So I don't know. If the preference is to get rid of substitutions it's a possibility. Not sure if there is a policy one way or another.

> Not sure if there is a policy one way or another.

I'm arguing more for consistency here: why natively call the one, and substitute the other? Nonetheless, fewer substitutions are also more desirable as they are easier to maintain ;)

> > Not sure if there is a policy one way or another.
> 
> I'm arguing more for consistency here: why natively call the one, and substitute the other? Nonetheless, fewer substitutions are also more desirable as they are easier to maintain ;)

I have no preference either way, so whatever is more desirable.
I reverted #5390 and verified that https://github.com/oracle/graal/issues/5387 is not re-introduced.

review_comment: Turns out the package is present on all platforms. Should we just add it to the `defaultBuiltInPkgNatives` list above?

The package is indeed present on all platforms, but as mentioned in https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/6740#pullrequestreview-1462799691 it only comes with native code on Linux.

I am OK with both approaches.
Let's not introduce any special handling here when not necessary.
